audit_findings.title: The FY2026 anchor appears inflated by a nonrecurring tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $47 million filed tax benefit, equal to 12.0% of the $391 million anchor; if fully retained, computed base value overstatement is approximately $14.70 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-time benefit increases the equity-level OE anchor and is capitalized through forecast earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: This decrease was primarily driven by a $47 million tax benefit related to an IRS audit settlement, pending final administrative approvals, covering fiscal years 2016 through 2019, and adjustments in liabilities for uncertain tax positions related to other open tax years.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2026 income included a $47 million IRS-settlement and uncertain-tax-position benefit. Whether the OE ledger removed it remains unresolved. Full retention would materially reduce normalized OE and could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2026 tax provision into the OE ledger, remove the $47 million settlement-related benefit if retained, preserve sustainable tax-law benefits, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: SilverEdge lacks a full-year perimeter normalization
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-year acquired-business contribution would increase OE, while full-year acquisition-financing interest and integration requirements would reduce OE; both affect the anchor rather than the debt bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 15, 2025, the Company acquired SilverEdge, an innovative provider of mission-driven technology solutions and products, for a preliminary purchase price of $ 203 million, net of $ 6 million cash acquired, subject to post-closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: FY2026 contains only $27 million of SilverEdge revenue following the October 2025 acquisition, while the subsequent six months contain $39 million. Filed data do not disclose SilverEdge owner earnings or incremental financing interest, so the net valuation effect and materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-year SilverEdge OE schedule from subsequent-quarter operating results and acquisition accounting, include full-year after-tax incremental interest, reconcile against consolidated results, and rerun the valuation without deducting debt principal.

audit_findings.title: An unquantified DOJ investigation could create a senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A fine or settlement would be an equity-bridge deduction or OE cash outflow; continuing defense costs would reduce OE, and sanctions or debarment could impair growth.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, it is not possible to determine whether the Company will incur, or to reasonably estimate the amount of, any fines, penalties or further liabilities in connection with the investigation pursuant to which the subpoenas were issued.
audit_findings.explanation: The investigation is an existing disclosed contingency, but both the 10-K and latest 10-Q state that possible fines, penalties, or further liabilities cannot be reasonably estimated. No demonstrated valuation error or material amount is established, although an omitted senior claim could reduce equity value.
audit_findings.action: Review each subsequent filing for resolution, accruals, defense costs, insurance or indemnification, and contract sanctions; rerun with a probability-weighted claim only when supportable amounts and probabilities become available.

audit_findings.title: A patent-settlement recovery may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $3 million filed net pretax settlement benefit ($9 million recovery less $6 million contingent costs), equal to 0.8% of the $391 million anchor; the gross recovery is 2.3% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpurged net settlement benefit increases the OE anchor and therefore forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: As part of the settlement, the Company was awarded $ 15 million and recognized $ 9 million as a recovery for costs previously incurred within "Selling, general and administrative expenses" within the Company’s consolidated statements of income during fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The recovery is demonstrably nonrecurring, but consistent treatment of the associated $6 million costs leaves only a $3 million net pretax benefit. Even the gross $9 million recovery is small relative to the anchor, the $30.72-$40.75 per-share scenario distances, and the 30% margin of safety.
audit_findings.action: Verify that the $9 million recovery and $6 million contingent costs received symmetrical nonrecurring treatment; correct the ledger if necessary, but no conclusion-changing rerun is indicated by the filed scale.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include uncleared payments
audit_findings.magnitude: $25 million filed at FY2026 year-end, equal to $0.56 per diluted share and 0.4% of base equity value; the July 2026 amount is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash that must clear against accounts payable is not distributable and should be excluded from the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company includes outstanding payments within "Cash and cash equivalents" and "Accounts payable" on the consolidated balance sheets and as of January 30, 2026 and January 31, 2025 these amounts were $ 25 million and $ 33 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The July amount is not disclosed, but the filed year-end amount is small. More conservatively, removing the entire $126 million July cash addition would reduce value by only $2.81 per share, or 2.2% of base value, and would not change the bear/base/bull relationship to the $126.75 market price or overcome the 30% margin of safety.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile July cash to outstanding payments, restricted cash, and required operating cash, then replace the bridge addition with separable cash; document the reconciliation even if no valuation-conclusion rerun is required.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.0 million residual, equal to 8.2% of the $391 million anchor; if entirely eligible, the computed base-value increase would be approximately $10.01 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A would be added back to OE, raising the anchor, forecast earnings, and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $32.0m (17.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving the residual as an expense is conservative and is not an overvaluation error. The $32 million envelope is potentially material, but the record does not establish what portion, if any, qualifies as a non-economic add-back, so actual materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the component-level D&A schedule, classify each residual item using filed asset lives and economic-replacement evidence, and rerun all scenarios only for the substantiated eligible portion.
